title: Monthly Step-Down Rate for a Hard-Worked Keyturn Vehicle Listing
content:
How hard a Keyturn Vehicle Listing has been worked since it was last valued, and how long it has been live, decide the rate at which its value steps down each whole month. The miles run since the valuation standing on the condition record and the months the listing has been live are read together.

| Miles run since the valuation standing on the condition record | Listing live for | Monthly rate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| more than 6000 miles | 36 whole months or more | nine thousandths (0.009) of the starting value a month |
| more than 6000 miles | fewer than 36 whole months | seven and a half thousandths (0.0075) a month |
| any other case | — | the standard rate |

As clauses: a vehicle that has run more than 6000 miles since the valuation standing on its condition record and whose listing has been live for 36 whole months or more steps down at nine thousandths of the starting value a month; one that has run more than 6000 miles since that valuation whose listing has been live for fewer than 36 whole months steps down at seven and a half thousandths a month; and any other vehicle steps down at the standard rate.

### Both sides of each figure

*The mileage test.* It is met above 6000 miles and not at it: a vehicle showing exactly 6000 miles run since that valuation falls to the last row whatever its age, and one showing 6001 miles is on one of the first two.

*The age test.* It is met at 36 whole months and above: a listing live for exactly 36 whole months takes the nine thousandths row, and one live for 35 whole months and 29 days takes the seven and a half thousandths row.
